relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - camelCase verb phrase for a narrower role deliberately carved out of a broader one by removing specific capabilities; a genuinely new but small predicate, not a new namespace
relations.evidence: Prior to 7.0.0 Eventing always run as "Full Admin" this blocked some use cases and adoption as this role allowed creation of new users and the ability to escalate privilege sets. The new "Eventing Full Admin" role removes the capability of creating users and modifying credentials thus providing a bit more security.

notable_absence.finding: Zero mentions of any capella-role:* or privilege:capella-advanced-access-* concept anywhere on this page - every access-control reference here is to the OTHER, classic-Couchbase-Server-RBAC role axis (Full Admin / Eventing Full Admin / generic 'admin privileges'), never to Capella's management-plane roles or Advanced-credential privileges documented in eventing-rbac.json. Confirms Eventing's access story runs on two genuinely separate, pre-existing systems side by side (Capella management-plane roles for the UI/credential surface; classic server RBAC roles for cluster-node-level admin operations like the recursion-check REST toggle and historical Eventing-as-Full-Admin bootstrapping) rather than unifying them or adding a third.

cross_component_finding: role:eventing-full-admin is the definitive fifth member of the role-naming-collision family documented in role:full-administrator's own promotion note (capella-role:*, rbac-role:role, sgw:role, role:full-administrator/role:local-user-security-administrator) - and critically, it is a NARROWER, PURPOSE-BUILT variant of an already-registered role (role:full-administrator), created specifically to give Eventing least-privilege bootstrapping without the ability to create users or escalate privileges. This is strong evidence against the round's 'new structural layer' hypothesis at the role-naming level too: Eventing's answer to 'we need a privileged role but not full admin' was to mint one narrower instance inside the SAME classic role: namespace, not to invent an Eventing-specific role system.
